carbon_policy_signal.item: UK and EU finalize Brexit agreement linking carbon emissions trading systems; expands eligible compliance instruments and reduces segmentation risk.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Broader compliance instrument eligibility lowers EUA-UKA arbitrage barriers, reduces ETS price discovery friction, and supports stable long-term curve pricing into 2027 — modest structural relief on segmentation tail-risk.

freshness_caveat: Coal metric stale as of 2025-12-26 (286 days old); Clean Dark stale as of 2025-12-31 (281 days old). Current coal price may not reflect recent thermal dispatch economics or Q4 2026 scarcity.
risk_flags: Storage 72.97% full, 15.1 pp below 5-yr seasonal norm — refill pace through winter will set H2 2027 power risk envelope.
Renewables at 21st-pctile (down 25% week-on-week) extend thermal merit-order call; if cold front materializes, gas call can spike hard.
Coal at 8th-percentile (96 USD/t, stale as of 26-Dec-2025) — lignite baseload protection intact but price signal may not reflect current scarcity.
France domestic fuel-price intervention mooted; state price caps or subsidies could suppress DA/Cal+1 spreads and distort cross-border arbs.

base.summary: Soft coal, weak renewables, tight storage sustain gas-to-power call; TTF stable, DE power tracks 84th-pctile range.

downside.summary: G7 reserve releases executed aggressively; crude/diesel margins collapse. Fuel-switch incentive evaporates, gas demand softens, TTF and DE power decline.

upside.summary: Cold front drives renewables below 15th-pctile; storage refill pace weakens. Gas-fired call surges, TTF rallies on winter heating demand.

themes: Tight EU gas, weak renewables forecast
G7 reserve releases dampen crude, ease fuel-switch pressure
EU-UK carbon linkage structural neutral, reduces ETS segmentation
DE/GB power elevated (84th/83rd pctile) despite soft coal economics
top_drivers: Renewables at 21st-pctile (down 25% week-on-week) extending thermal call; storage 15 pp below seasonal tightens gas-to-power transmission.
G7 crude reserve releases and record US LNG supply dampen refined margins and cap fuel-switch incentive — TTF downside lever if implemented aggressively.
EU-UK carbon linkage finalizes — reduces ETS segmentation, neutral to modest EUA relief on broader eligibility; structural pricing effect into 2027 curve.
top_takeaway: Storage 15 pp below seasonal, renewables at 21st-pctile, and TTF +3.2% daily signal tight autumn gas regime; G7 reserve releases and record US LNG supply cap upside.

watchlist.why: 72.97% full vs 15.1 pp below seasonal average; November–January injection/withdrawal will determine H1 2027 gas-power tightness.

watchlist.metric: G7 crude reserve releases — timing & volume
watchlist.why: Bearish diesel/refined margins → reduces fuel-switch incentive from gas → TTF downside if drawn down aggressively in Nov–Dec.

watchlist.metric: US LNG export ramp (record July 2026 production)
watchlist.why: Higher US supply available to EU; lower LNG scarcity premium caps TTF arbitrage upside; monitor cargo flow data.

watchlist.metric: France intervention measures (price caps, subsidy scope)
watchlist.why: Domestic policy may suppress EDF/gas-fired margins and distort cross-border power-gas spread arbs; watch for legislative signals.
US crude margins elevated on geopolitical premium; any Hormuz disruption will reverse bearish refined-product pressure and trigger fuel-switch rally.

watchlist_dated.name: IEA assessment (oil reserve release trigger)
watchlist_dated.why: Determines EU eligibility for further strategic stock releases post-March accord; timing shapes crude/diesel arb into Nov–Dec.
